::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 1st 1892  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear Mr Archdeacon[^1]
I am venturing to ask a favour of you.

I do not know whether you have heard of the [Mother’s Union](organizations/other_31.qmd), started by [Mrs G Sumner](people/person_1381.qmd) (the wife of the [Bishop of Guildford](people/person_1382.qmd)) at first for poor women, to rouse them to some heed to the training of their children but it gradually spread to ladies &c. and indeed quite as much counsel seems to be needed by them as by cottage women.

The need of an ‘organ’ was soon felt, and <u>faute de mieux</u>, I have had to edit the quarterly [‘Mothers in Council’](organizations/other_82.qmd) of which I send a specimen.

We want particularly good advice upon boys’ training. Some excellent papers we have had, and we should be very grateful if you would give us a short paper on some point in their home training. What is foremost in my mind is the fore-arming against the many temptations to gambling - but for any other subject that you might prefer, we should be grateful. I am afraid at present that it must be gratitude alone, as [Wells Gardiner](organizations/other_114.qmd) who publishes at the risk of the President does not yet pay beyond the expenses, though the sale encreases [sic]

I remain
Yours very truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: CMY is evidently writing to someone who is not a stranger to her from outside the diocese of Winchester. A possible candidate is the Rev. [William Emery](people/person_2107.qmd) (1825-1910), Archdeacon of Ely, who was interested in schools, and whom CMY knew because he was involved in the Church Congresses.
